# @vllnt/typescript

> Shared tsconfig presets for Node.js apps, npm libraries, React and Next.js, with strict type-checking, tested with TypeScript 6 and 7.

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@vllnt/typescript
- Repository: https://github.com/vllnt/typescript
- Documentation: [README](./README.md)
- API reference: [API](./README.md#api)
- Errors and fixes: [Errors and fixes](./README.md#errors-and-fixes)
- Changelog: [CHANGELOG](./CHANGELOG.md)
- License: MIT

Install independently in any project; no vllnt monorepo is required. npm latest
is stable 3.0.1 at this audit; canary is a moving prerelease channel. Pin and test
prereleases. See [Contributing](https://github.com/vllnt/typescript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Security policy](https://github.com/vllnt/typescript/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## For coding agents

The documentation ships inside the package: `node_modules/@vllnt/typescript/` contains `README.md`, `llms.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md` next to the preset files, and they match the installed version. The package contains only JSON presets for `extends`; there is no JavaScript or type export to import.

## When to use

- Use it when one `extends` line should set the compiler options of a Node.js app, an npm library, a bundled React app or a Next.js app.
- Use it when the project compiles with TypeScript 7, or with TypeScript 6.0.2 or newer.
- Do not use it on TypeScript 5 or older, or when you need ES5 output: use a `@tsconfig/*` preset that matches your compiler, such as `@tsconfig/node22`, or write your own `tsconfig.json`.
- Do not use it when the code cannot pass `strict` plus the extra flags of `base.json`: write your own `tsconfig.json`, or start from `@tsconfig/recommended`.

## Install

`pnpm add --save-dev @vllnt/typescript typescript@^7`, then extend one preset, such as `"extends": "@vllnt/typescript/nodejs.json"`.

## Compatibility

- Node.js consumers: 22 or newer
- TypeScript: `>=6.0.2 <8`
- TypeScript 7 migration: native `tsc` can run beside the TypeScript 6 compatibility API
- Runtime dependencies: none; TypeScript is a peer dependency

## Presets

Extend one preset per project; every preset extends `base.json`. Full option lists: [API](./README.md#api).

- `@vllnt/typescript/base.json`: strict shared defaults and explicit ambient types; sets no `module`, `target` or `lib`
- `@vllnt/typescript/nodejs.json`: Node.js applications; NodeNext, ES2024, emits declarations and source maps
- `@vllnt/typescript/node-library.json`: publishable npm packages; as `nodejs.json` plus `declarationMap` (declaration maps)
- `@vllnt/typescript/react.json`: bundled React applications; ESNext with Bundler resolution, ES2022, DOM libs, `jsx: "react-jsx"`, emits declarations and source maps; set `noEmit: true` when a bundler such as Vite emits
- `@vllnt/typescript/nextjs.json`: Next.js applications; ESNext with Bundler resolution, ES2022, DOM libs, `jsx: "preserve"`, `noEmit`, `incremental`, `allowJs`, the `next` plugin

Consumers should list required ambient packages in `types` and set `rootDir` in emitting projects.
Emitting presets do not enable `incremental`, so a clean build emits every output even when a `.tsbuildinfo` file is left over. Projects that set `incremental: true` should delete the `.tsbuildinfo` file with the output directory before a clean build.

## Strictness inherited from base.json

Every preset enables `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUncheckedSideEffectImports`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. The diagnostic codes and fixes are in [Errors and fixes](./README.md#errors-and-fixes).

Migrating from version 2 (the last four flags are new):

- `noImplicitOverride` (TS4114): add `override` to a method that replaces a base-class method.
- `noImplicitReturns` (TS7030): return on every path; use `return undefined;` when that is intended.
- `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` (TS7029): end a non-empty `case` with `break`, `return` or `throw`.
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (TS2375, TS2379, TS2412): write `prop?: T | undefined` where `undefined` is a valid value, or omit the key.
- JavaScript output does not change. Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, inferred declarations can: `count?: number | undefined` is emitted as `count?: number`.
- To adopt them gradually, set a flag to `false` in the project's own `compilerOptions` after `extends`.

## Related packages

- [@vllnt/eslint-config](https://oss.vllnt.com/packages/eslint-config): ESLint presets for TypeScript projects; lint rules, configured separately from these compiler presets.
